purpose: A per-business deep-research protocol for independent Turlock and Stanislaus County shops that captures a canonical sourced profile (identity, service lines, ownership and longevity, size signals, supply chain, demand, economics, online presence, and regulatory footprint), models supply chain by trade and revenue strictly as a labeled benchmark estimate scaled by observable size signals, scores per-field and per-profile confidence with provenance, registers what could not be verified, gates each profile for publication and specialist-grounding quality, aggregates passing profiles into category insight, and spawns a category specialist through the FACTORY pipeline once a category holds enough quality profiles.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all benchmarks, bands, and scores are reasoned heuristic priors and labeled estimates, not quotes or actuals
per-business revenue and profit for private independent shops are not public and are modeled only as labeled benchmark estimates, never stated as fact
only public business data is used (FBN filings, license registries, Google/social profiles, assessor parcels); no private or personal data on owners beyond public records
the geography is Turlock / Stanislaus County within the Modesto MSA, profiling independent (non-chain) businesses
the upstream business catalog and category taxonomy already exist (kb1 discovery and kb2 taxonomy); this KB is the per-business profiling layer beneath them
exclusions: discovering or enumerating which businesses exist — covered by the discovery-methodology KB
defining the category scheme and assignment rules — covered by the categorization-taxonomy KB
stating any named business's actual revenue, profit, or private financials as fact
collecting private or personal data on owners beyond public business-registration records
authoring the downstream category specialist's content itself (this KB only defines the spawn trigger and pipeline hand-off)

competency_questions.question: What is the goal of a business profile and what makes it good enough to be both standalone-useful and to ground a category specialist?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROFILING_GOAL states the dual purpose and the per-claim source-and-confidence rule; PROFILE_QA_GATE defines the grounding-quality bar

competency_questions.question: What is the canonical profile schema and which sections must every business record contain?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROFILE_SCHEMA enumerates the fixed sections and the empty-becomes-unknown rule

competency_questions.question: How are a business's service lines captured and sourced rather than guessed from its name?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SERVICE_LINES lists discrete lines tagged core/peripheral with the menu/site/profile/photo/review source for each

competency_questions.question: How are ownership and operating longevity established from public records and durable signals?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OWNERSHIP_LONGEVITY uses the FBN registrant/date, 'since YYYY', and review-history span as bracketing proxies using only public data

competency_questions.question: Which observable size signals are recorded and how do they scale economic estimates without being revenue themselves?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SIZE_SIGNALS records sqft, headcount, hours, locations, review volume, and seating/bays as sourced proxies, not revenue

competency_questions.question: How is the supply chain modeled — both the trade input pattern and the specific suppliers?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SUPPLY_CHAIN_PATTERN maps typical inputs per trade and SUPPLIER_ID localizes them to named or typed-candidate suppliers with confidence

competency_questions.question: How is the customer base and demand profile (B2C/B2B, local/regional, community-specific) characterized?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEMAND_PROFILE states the B2C/B2B mix, the local-vs-regional draw, and community-specific demand with evidence

competency_questions.question: How is per-trade seasonality captured and why does it matter for any annualized estimate?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SEASONALITY describes the trade's peaks/troughs and the annualization caution

competency_questions.question: How is competitive position and differentiation captured and why is it provisional until peers are profiled?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPETITIVE_POSITION records price tier, specialization, and relative reputation, flagged provisional until aggregation

competency_questions.question: How is revenue estimated so that it is always a labeled estimate and never a stated fact about a named business?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REVENUE_ESTIMATE emits a benchmark-times-size low-mid-high band tagged 'estimate, not actual' with confidence and a confirmation note

competency_questions.question: How is cost structure and margin modeled as a labeled benchmark rather than the business's actual books?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COST_MARGIN gives a labeled trade cost-split and net-margin band used to sanity-check revenue, never asserted as real profit

competency_questions.question: How are online presence/channel mix and the per-trade regulatory footprint captured and used as proxies, differentiators, and category cross-checks?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ONLINE_PRESENCE records Google profile state, social scale, website, and ordering channels with sources, and REGULATORY_FOOTPRINT lists the trade's public licenses/registries used to corroborate identity and category

competency_questions.question: How are confidence and provenance scored per field and per profile, how are unverified facts registered, and how is the no-stated-private-financials guardrail enforced?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONFIDENCE_SCORING assigns per-field tiers with source tags and a weakest-link profile rollup, UNKNOWNS_REGISTER lists each unverified field with its closing evidence, and REVENUE_GUARDRAIL forbids any unlabeled named-business financial figure and any private owner data

competency_questions.question: How is a profile gated for publication and specialist-grounding, how are passing profiles aggregated, when is a category specialist spawned via the FACTORY pipeline, and how is the catalog maintained?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROFILE_QA_GATE issues a pass/provisional/fail verdict, CATEGORY_AGGREGATION rolls up distributions, supplier hubs, and refined benchmarks, SPAWN_PROTOCOL spawns only on >= K grounding-quality profiles plus coverage via the full forge+gate+specialist-gate pipeline, and CATALOG_MAINTENANCE re-profiles on new-info/closure/ownership-change/pivot/staleness triggers

glossary.definition: A 'doing business as' statement filed with the Stanislaus County Clerk-Recorder that publicly records the registrant and filing date; used here as the primary public proxy for ownership and a lower bound on longevity.
An industry figure for annual sales divided by headcount; multiplied by an estimated staff count it yields a labeled revenue band when square footage is unavailable.
An industry figure for annual sales per square foot of selling/operating space; multiplied by an estimated footprint it yields a labeled revenue band, the primary method for retail and food service.
An observable, non-financial proxy for scale (square footage, headcount, hours, location count, review volume, seating or bay count) that is multiplied against benchmarks but is never itself revenue.
A supplier recorded by type ('regional foodservice distributor') rather than by name when no specific supplier can be evidenced, carried at a confidence that reflects the inference.
A profile that passes the QA gate at the higher bar required to count toward spawning a category specialist, as opposed to a 'provisional' profile that may publish but does not ground a specialist.
The rule that a profile's overall confidence equals the confidence of its weakest load-bearing field, not an average, so a single solid field cannot mask several guesses.
The mandatory tag on every economic figure for a named business, declaring it a benchmark-derived estimate with a confidence and a confirmation path, never a stated fact.

A supplier (e.g. a local tortilleria or a regional foodservice distributor) that recurs across many profiles in a category, surfaced only at the aggregation layer and used to refine supply-chain inference.
The age past which a profile's load-bearing fields are re-verified during catalog maintenance even absent any event trigger, keeping benchmarks and facts current.

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for a Turlock independent-business deep-profiling protocol, informed by public business-registration practice (Stanislaus County FBN), California trade licensing registries (BAR, CSLB, ABC, Board of Barbering and Cosmetology), Google Business and social-profile signals, county assessor parcel data, and published industry revenue-per-employee and revenue-per-square-foot benchmarks used only as labeled estimates; no supplied dataset and no private financial data
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Stanislaus County Clerk-Recorder Fictitious Business Name (FBN) filings; California Bureau of Automotive Repair (BAR), Contractors State License Board (CSLB), Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC), and Board of Barbering and Cosmetology license registries; Google Business Profile and Instagram/Facebook public signals; Stanislaus County Assessor parcel records; U.S. Census County Business Patterns and published RMA/industry revenue-per-employee and revenue-per-sqft benchmarks used as labeled estimates; heuristic priors where no dataset is supplied

nodes.definition: Produce one deep, fully sourced profile per independent Turlock business that is simultaneously useful on its own (a reader knows what the shop sells, who runs it, how big it is, and roughly how it makes money) and rich enough to ground a category specialist once several peers are profiled. The profile is a research artifact, not marketing copy: every claim carries a source and a confidence, and absence of evidence is recorded rather than papered over.

included: the dual purpose: standalone usefulness plus specialist-grounding

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the profiling purpose or downstream grounding requirement is restated

pros.claim: Fixing the dual purpose up front stops profiles from drifting into shallow directory listings that cannot ground a specialist
pros.example: a profile that records only name, address, and phone is useless for later supply-chain or revenue aggregation

cons.claim: Holding every profile to specialist-grounding depth slows throughput when a thin listing would have sufficed for a directory
cons.example: spending an hour sourcing supply chain for a shop that is about to close

failure_modes: profiles written as promotional blurbs with no provenance
depth so uneven across a category that aggregation is impossible
acceptance_tests: the goal statement names both the standalone-usefulness and specialist-grounding purposes and asserts the per-claim source-and-confidence rule
revisit_triggers: the downstream specialist-spawn criteria change
a category proves to need a field the goal never anticipated

nodes.definition: Define the canonical profile record with fixed sections so every business is captured comparably: identity (legal/DBA name, FBN reference), location (address, district, single vs multi-site), service lines (what they sell), ownership and longevity, size signals, supply-chain pattern, demand and customer base, economics (labeled revenue and margin estimates), online presence and channel mix, regulatory footprint, a confidence block, and an unknowns register. The schema is the contract every other node fills; a field left empty must be marked unknown, never silently dropped.

included: the rule that empty fields become explicit unknowns
excluded: how each individual field is sourced

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a required profile section is added, removed, or restructured

pros.claim: A fixed schema makes profiles diffable and aggregatable, which is what later category roll-up depends on
pros.example: every profile having a size-signal block lets the aggregator compute a category sqft distribution

cons.claim: A rigid schema can force awkward fits for businesses that straddle categories or have unusual structures
cons.example: a combined panaderia-and-restaurant whose single service-line field cannot hold both cleanly

failure_modes: fields silently omitted instead of marked unknown, hiding gaps
schema drift between profilers so two records are not comparable
acceptance_tests: the schema enumerates every required section (identity, location, lines, ownership, size, supply chain, demand, economics, online, regulatory, confidence, unknowns) and states the empty-becomes-unknown rule
revisit_triggers: a category repeatedly needs a section the schema lacks
the aggregation layer requests a new structured field

nodes.definition: Capture exactly what the business sells or does as a discrete list of service lines, sourced from the business's own menu, website, Google Business profile categories, posted photos, and review text rather than guessed from the name. A taqueria's lines are tacos/burritos/catering; an auto shop's are smog/brakes/diagnostics; a boutique's are apparel/accessories. Each line should note whether it is a core revenue driver or a peripheral add-on, because that distinction drives both the revenue and supply-chain models.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the business's offerings or their evidence change

pros.claim: Sourcing lines from menus and review photos rather than the business name avoids miscategorizing a place that has quietly diversified
pros.example: a 'tire shop' whose reviews reveal half its revenue is now used-car sales

cons.claim: Review-mined lines can over-weight whatever customers happened to photograph, missing quiet high-margin services
cons.example: a salon's reviews show haircuts but never its more profitable color and keratin work

failure_modes: inferring lines from the trade name and missing actual offerings
listing every trivial item so the core driver is lost in noise
acceptance_tests: service lines are listed as discrete items, each tagged core or peripheral, with the source (menu, site, profile, photo, or review) cited for each
revisit_triggers: the business adds, drops, or re-emphasizes a service line
new menu or photo evidence contradicts the recorded lines

nodes.definition: Establish ownership and operating longevity from public records and durable signals: the Fictitious Business Name (FBN) filing at the Stanislaus County Clerk-Recorder (registrant and file date), any 'serving Turlock since YYYY' on signage or site, the span of the review history (first review date as a lower bound on age), and ownership-change cues. Only public business-registration data is used; no private or personal data on owners beyond what the FBN and public filings already disclose. Longevity is a proxy for stability and accumulated local demand.

included: review-history span as an age lower bound
excluded: personal data on owners beyond public filings

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an FBN, ownership, or longevity signal changes

pros.claim: An FBN file date plus first-review date brackets a business's true age far better than any single signal
pros.example: a 2009 FBN filing and a 2011 first review put a shop's local tenure at well over a decade

cons.claim: FBN filings lapse, get re-filed, or list a holding registrant, so they can mislead on continuity and true operator
cons.example: a re-filed FBN making a 30-year business look five years old

failure_modes: treating a recent FBN re-filing as the founding date
crossing the line into private owner data not in public filings
acceptance_tests: ownership and longevity cite at least the FBN registrant/date or an equivalent public record plus one corroborating durable signal, using only public data
revisit_triggers: a new FBN filing or ownership transfer appears
signage or profile reveals a different founding year

nodes.definition: Record the observable size proxies that scale every economic estimate: storefront square footage (from assessor parcel data, satellite/Street View footprint, or leasing listings), staff headcount (from photos, reviews mentioning staff, hours coverage), operating hours and days, number of locations, review volume and velocity as a demand proxy, and seating count or bay count for restaurants and auto shops. None of these is revenue, but together they are the size vector the revenue and margin models multiply against benchmarks.

included: sqft, headcount, hours, location count, review volume, seating/bays
excluded: converting size to revenue (that is the revenue node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an observable size signal changes

pros.claim: A multi-signal size vector lets revenue be triangulated even when one proxy is missing
pros.example: no sqft available, but bay count and staff headcount still scale an auto-shop estimate

cons.claim: Size proxies are noisy and can mislead — a large footprint may be mostly storage, a high review count may be old
cons.example: a cavernous antique store with low staffing and slow turnover looking bigger than it earns

failure_modes: reading gross footprint as sellable/productive space
treating lifetime review count as current demand without checking velocity
acceptance_tests: at least three size signals are recorded with a source each, and each is labeled as a size proxy not a revenue figure
revisit_triggers: the business expands, downsizes, or opens/closes a location
staffing or hours visibly change

nodes.definition: Model the typical upstream inputs for the business's trade as a pattern before naming any specific supplier: a panaderia needs flour, sugar, shortening, and packaging; a taqueria needs tortillas (often a local tortilleria), meat from a wholesale butcher or restaurant-depot, and produce; an auto shop needs parts (jobber/warehouse distributors), fluids, and tires; a boutique needs apparel from wholesale markets or brand distributors; a salon needs professional product lines and equipment. The pattern is the category-level input map that the supplier-identification node then localizes.

included: the pattern as a template for supplier localization

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the trade's typical input pattern or the business's lines change

pros.claim: A trade input pattern lets a profiler reason about supply chain even with zero direct evidence from the business
pros.example: knowing every taqueria needs a tortilla source directs the search before any supplier is confirmed

cons.claim: Generic trade patterns miss idiosyncratic sourcing that defines a particular business
cons.example: a bakery that mills its own flour, breaking the assumed wholesale-flour input

failure_modes: applying a generic pattern so rigidly that a distinctive input is missed
mapping inputs to the wrong service line
acceptance_tests: the typical upstream input categories for the trade are listed and linked to the service lines they feed
revisit_triggers: a service line is added that changes the input set
evidence shows the business sources atypically

nodes.definition: Localize the supply-chain pattern into named or typed suppliers using public evidence: delivery-truck branding in photos, distributor logos on shelves or equipment, restaurant-depot and cash-and-carry proximity (e.g. a regional Smart Foodservice / Restaurant Depot serving the Central Valley), local tortillerias and wholesale produce houses, auto-parts jobber networks, and the wholesale apparel and beauty-distribution channels that serve the Valley. Where a specific supplier cannot be evidenced, the supplier is recorded as a typed candidate ('regional foodservice distributor') with the confidence that reflects the inference.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new supplier evidence or a category supplier hub emerges

pros.claim: Photo-mined distributor branding can confirm a real supplier link no directory would reveal
pros.example: a delivery truck logo in a review photo naming the bakery's flour distributor

cons.claim: Visible branding shows one supplier on one day and can misrepresent the primary sourcing relationship
cons.example: a one-off cash-and-carry run photographed and mistaken for the standing supplier

failure_modes: asserting a named supplier from a single ambiguous photo
omitting the typed-candidate fallback and leaving supply chain blank
acceptance_tests: each major input has either an evidenced named supplier or a typed candidate, each with a source and a confidence reflecting the inference strength
revisit_triggers: new photo or shelf evidence of a distributor appears
a category supplier hub is identified during aggregation

nodes.definition: Characterize who buys and why: business-to-consumer vs business-to-business mix, local-neighborhood vs regional/destination draw, and community-specific demand (e.g. an Assyrian or Mexican grocer serving a specific community, a quinceanera dress shop serving regional events). Evidence comes from review-author geography and language, the product mix, hours patterns, and whether the business advertises wholesale or catering. The demand profile explains the revenue model's volume side and flags businesses whose demand is narrow and defensible versus broad and contested.

included: evidence from reviews and product mix

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the customer base or demand evidence changes

pros.claim: Identifying a defensible community-specific demand explains durability a generic category model would miss
pros.example: a halal market whose regional draw insulates it from a nearby chain grocer

cons.claim: Inferring customer geography from review authorship is biased toward who writes reviews, not who buys
cons.example: an older clientele that never posts reviews making a busy shop look quiet and local-only

failure_modes: assuming B2C when a quiet storefront actually runs on B2B wholesale
reading reviewer language as the whole customer base
acceptance_tests: the demand profile states the B2C/B2B mix, the local-vs-regional draw, and any community-specific demand, each with its evidence
revisit_triggers: the product or customer mix shifts
a wholesale or catering line appears or disappears

nodes.definition: Record the demand cycle each trade rides: a panaderia peaks at Dia de los Muertos and the holidays; a dress/formalwear shop peaks in quinceanera and prom season; an auto shop sees pre-summer and pre-winter service spikes; a tax-prep office is intensely seasonal Jan-April; ag-support businesses follow harvest. Seasonality is sourced from review-volume timing, posted seasonal products, and trade knowledge. It is essential because a single-month observation of size or demand can badly misread an annualized estimate.

included: sourcing from review timing and seasonal products

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new seasonal evidence or a seasonal line changes the cycle

pros.claim: Knowing the seasonal shape prevents annualizing a peak-month or trough-month snapshot into a wrong yearly figure
pros.example: reading a tax office's April rush as its steady state and overstating annual revenue threefold

cons.claim: Review-timing seasonality is a weak signal because review posting lags and clusters unevenly
cons.example: a holiday rush that generates reviews in January, smearing the apparent peak

failure_modes: annualizing a single peak or trough observation
missing a sharp seasonal trade like tax prep or formalwear
acceptance_tests: the trade's seasonal peaks and troughs are described with their evidence and an explicit note on how seasonality adjusts any annualized estimate
revisit_triggers: a full year of review data refines the cycle
the business adds a seasonal line

nodes.definition: Capture how the business is positioned against local peers and what differentiates it: price tier (value/mid/premium from menu prices and review sentiment), specialization or signature offering, reputation strength (rating and review volume relative to category peers), and moat sources (community ties, location, longevity, a unique product). This both sharpens the standalone profile and feeds category aggregation, since differentiation is only legible once several peers are profiled side by side.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the competitive set or the business's positioning changes

pros.claim: Relative reputation (rating vs category peers) is more informative than a raw star count
pros.example: a 4.3-star taqueria standing out only once the local taqueria median is seen to be 3.9

cons.claim: Differentiation judged before peers are profiled is speculative and may invert after aggregation
cons.example: calling a price 'premium' before the category's price distribution is known

failure_modes: asserting differentiation with no peer baseline
confusing a loud marketing claim with a real moat
acceptance_tests: competitive position records a price tier, a specialization, and a relative-reputation note, each grounded in evidence, with peer comparison flagged as provisional until aggregation
revisit_triggers: enough category peers are profiled to set a real baseline
a competitor opens or closes nearby

nodes.definition: Estimate revenue ONLY as a labeled band, never as a stated fact about a named business, because per-business revenue for private shops is not public. The method: pick an industry benchmark (revenue-per-employee or revenue-per-square-foot for the trade), multiply by the observed size signals, adjust for seasonality and demand draw, and emit a low-mid-high band tagged 'estimate, not actual' with an explicit confidence level and a 'what would confirm it' note (e.g. sales-tax permit data, a public franchise disclosure, an owner interview). Any figure not so labeled is a defect.

included: mandatory estimate label, confidence, and confirmation note

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a benchmark, size signal, or confirming data point changes

pros.claim: A benchmark-times-size band gives a defensible order-of-magnitude without ever fabricating a private figure
pros.example: a 1,800 sqft cafe at a foodservice revenue-per-sqft benchmark yields a labeled band, not a fake exact number

cons.claim: Benchmark bands can be wide to the point of low usefulness when size signals are thin
cons.example: a band spanning 2x because only a rough footprint is known

failure_modes: emitting a single point figure instead of a band
dropping the 'estimate, not actual' label or the confirmation note
acceptance_tests: every revenue output is a low-mid-high band tagged 'estimate, not actual' with a stated benchmark source, a confidence level, and a 'what would confirm it' note; no point figure is presented as fact
revisit_triggers: a better benchmark or size signal becomes available
a confirming public data point (e.g. tax permit) surfaces

nodes.definition: Model the trade's cost structure and typical margin as a labeled benchmark, never as the named business's actual books: food-service runs ~28-35% food cost and thin net margins; salons are labor-and-product heavy; auto shops split parts and labor margin; retail boutiques live on keystone-ish markup against rent. The output is a benchmark margin pattern with the same estimate discipline as revenue — a band, a confidence, and a confirmation note — used to sanity-check the revenue band and to characterize how the business likely makes money, not to assert its profit.

included: trade benchmark cost split and net-margin pattern

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a trade cost benchmark or input-cost condition changes

pros.claim: A trade margin benchmark catches a revenue band that implies an impossible profit and forces a re-check
pros.example: a revenue estimate that would imply a restaurant nets 40% flags the size signal as overstated

cons.claim: Margin benchmarks vary so widely within a trade that the band is more illustrative than precise
cons.example: two salons with the same revenue but very different rent and commission structures

failure_modes: presenting a benchmark margin as the business's real profit
ignoring local cost factors like Valley rent
acceptance_tests: cost structure is a labeled benchmark band (cost split plus net-margin pattern) with a confidence and confirmation note, explicitly not the business's actual books
revisit_triggers: a trade benchmark is refined by aggregated profiles
input-cost conditions shift materially

nodes.definition: Map the digital footprint and channel mix: Google Business profile (claimed/unclaimed, rating, review count, photos, posts), Instagram/Facebook activity and follower scale, a website or its absence, and ordering/booking channels (DoorDash/UberEats, online ordering, Square/booking apps). Channel mix is both a size/demand proxy and a differentiator — an unclaimed Google profile and no website signal a traditional, referral-driven operation, while active Instagram and third-party ordering signal a younger, broader-reach business.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the business's online channels or activity change

pros.claim: Channel mix doubles as evidence for size, demand, and differentiation at almost no extra research cost
pros.example: a verified profile with 600 reviews and active Instagram corroborates strong demand independently

cons.claim: Digital absence is not business absence — many durable Valley shops run almost entirely offline
cons.example: a 30-year carniceria with no website and a sparse profile that nonetheless dominates its block

failure_modes: equating a thin online footprint with a weak business
double-counting online reviews already used as a size signal without noting the overlap
acceptance_tests: the online block records Google profile state, any social channels with scale, website presence, and ordering/booking channels, each with a source
revisit_triggers: the business claims a profile, launches a site, or adds an ordering channel
social activity materially changes

nodes.definition: Record the licensing and regulatory footprint typical of the trade, which ties each profile back to its category: a restaurant needs a Stanislaus County health permit and ABC license if it serves alcohol; an auto shop needs a BAR (Bureau of Automotive Repair) registration and a smog license; a salon needs a Board of Barbering and Cosmetology establishment license; a contractor needs a CSLB license. These are public registries that both confirm legitimacy and provide an additional sourcing channel for identity, longevity, and category assignment.

included: licenses as a legitimacy and sourcing channel

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a license status or the trade's regulatory regime changes

pros.claim: Public license registries (BAR, CSLB, ABC, cosmetology board) are an authoritative cross-check on identity and category
pros.example: a CSLB lookup confirming a contractor's license class and active status and founding-era issue date

cons.claim: License presence confirms a trade but not scale, and a missing license may reflect a sub-trade not the absence of one
cons.example: a home baker with no health permit who is a cottage-food operator, not unlicensed

failure_modes: treating a missing public license as proof of illegitimacy
ignoring the registry as a free corroboration source
acceptance_tests: the trade's expected public licenses/registries are listed, checked where lookupable, and used to corroborate identity and category
revisit_triggers: a license is issued, lapses, or changes class
the trade's regulatory regime changes

nodes.definition: Score confidence at two levels with explicit provenance: each field carries a confidence (high if from a public record or the business's own channel, medium if from corroborated reviews/photos, low if inferred from trade pattern) and a source tag; the profile carries a rolled-up confidence that is gated by its weakest load-bearing fields, not an average. Provenance — the specific source behind each claim — is mandatory, so a reader can audit any assertion and the aggregation layer can weight profiles by reliability.

included: per-field confidence tiers and source tags

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a field's provenance or the confidence rollup rule changes

pros.claim: A weakest-link rollup stops a profile with one solid field and five guesses from looking trustworthy
pros.example: a profile with a confirmed FBN but guessed revenue, supplier, and demand scoring low overall, not medium-high

cons.claim: Per-field scoring adds overhead that can be skipped under time pressure, eroding the whole discipline
cons.example: a profiler tagging everything 'medium' to move faster, defeating the scheme

failure_modes: averaging confidence so weak fields are hidden
claims with no source tag, making provenance unauditable
acceptance_tests: every field has a confidence tier and a source tag, and the profile confidence is set by its weakest load-bearing field, not an average
revisit_triggers: a field's source is upgraded or downgraded
the rollup rule is found to mis-rank profiles

nodes.definition: Maintain an explicit register of what could not be verified, so absence of evidence is recorded as data rather than guessed over: unknown founding year, unconfirmed primary supplier, unobservable headcount, unverifiable revenue beyond the benchmark band. Each unknown notes what was attempted and what evidence would close it. This register is what keeps the profile honest, feeds the confidence rollup, and gives the next researcher a precise to-do list instead of a blank.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an unknown is resolved or a new gap is found

pros.claim: A populated unknowns register turns gaps into a targeted research backlog instead of silent holes
pros.example: 'primary tortilla supplier unconfirmed; would be closed by a delivery-photo or owner statement'

cons.claim: An over-long unknowns list can signal a profile too thin to be worth publishing yet
cons.example: a register longer than the verified facts, indicating the business needs more research before use

failure_modes: filling unknowns with plausible guesses instead of marking them unknown
leaving the register empty when fields were in fact unverified
acceptance_tests: the register lists each unverified material field with what was attempted and what evidence would resolve it
revisit_triggers: an unknown is resolved by new evidence
a previously confident field is called into doubt

nodes.definition: Apply the acceptance gate that decides whether a profile is good enough to publish and to count toward grounding a category specialist. The gate requires: identity and category confirmed from at least one public record; service lines sourced not guessed; at least three size signals; a labeled revenue band with confirmation note; a populated confidence block; and a profile confidence at or above a set threshold (weak-but-honest profiles may publish as 'provisional' but do not count toward specialist-grounding). The gate is the sole predecessor of publication and of the spawn count.

included: gate as sole predecessor of publish and spawn-count
excluded: the aggregation that uses passing profiles

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the acceptance criteria or grounding-quality bar changes

pros.claim: A hard gate keeps thin or unsourced profiles from silently corrupting the category benchmark and the future specialist
pros.example: a guessed-revenue, name-only profile blocked from counting toward the spawn threshold

cons.claim: A strict gate slows coverage and may exclude small obscure businesses that are simply under-documented publicly
cons.example: a cash-only home-based seamstress with almost no public footprint failing the gate despite being real

failure_modes: letting a profile count toward spawn despite failing confidence
applying the gate inconsistently across profilers
acceptance_tests: each profile receives a pass / provisional / fail verdict against the explicit criteria, and only passing profiles count toward specialist-grounding
revisit_triggers: the spawn threshold or grounding-quality bar changes
a published profile is later found defective

nodes.definition: Aggregate passing profiles within a category into rolling insights: the distribution of size signals and labeled revenue bands, recurring supplier hubs (a tortilleria or foodservice distributor named across many profiles), refined trade benchmarks (tightening revenue-per-sqft once N local examples exist), common seasonal and demand patterns, and the competitive landscape. Aggregation both improves every individual profile's benchmarks (a feedback loop) and produces the category-level knowledge a specialist will stand on.

included: distributions, supplier hubs, refined benchmarks, shared patterns

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new passing profiles enter the category or a benchmark is refined

pros.claim: Aggregating real local profiles tightens benchmarks far beyond generic national figures
pros.example: ten profiled taquerias yielding a local revenue-per-seat band specific to Turlock

cons.claim: Aggregating across a thin or biased sample bakes early sampling errors into the category benchmark
cons.example: five upscale restaurants skewing the 'Turlock restaurant' benchmark high before mid-tier ones are profiled

failure_modes: refining a benchmark on too few or unrepresentative profiles
missing a recurring supplier hub visible only across profiles
acceptance_tests: the category roll-up reports size and revenue-band distributions, named recurring supplier hubs, and at least one refined benchmark, with the sample size stated
revisit_triggers: new passing profiles are added to the category
a benchmark refinement is contradicted by fresh data

nodes.definition: Define the protocol that spawns a category specialist once a category holds at least K grounding-quality profiles (e.g. K=8) with adequate coverage of its size and price range: emit the category specialist through the same FACTORY pipeline used here — forge three dense KBs for the category (its discovery, its taxonomy depth, its profiling/economics), gate each at EXIT=0, then distill and gate the specialist. The spawn is gated by both profile quantity and aggregation quality, never by count alone, so a specialist never stands on thin or skewed evidence.

included: the K-quality-profiles threshold plus coverage condition
emission via the FACTORY 3-KB + specialist pipeline

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the spawn threshold, coverage rule, or pipeline changes

pros.claim: Gating the spawn on aggregation quality, not just a profile count, stops premature specialists built on biased samples
pros.example: holding back a 'restaurant specialist' until mid-tier and ethnic eateries are represented, not just the eight easiest to profile

cons.claim: A high threshold delays useful specialists for small but coherent categories that will never reach K
cons.example: a niche like saddle-and-tack shops that has only three local businesses total

failure_modes: spawning on raw count while coverage is skewed
skipping the FACTORY gate steps and emitting an ungated specialist
acceptance_tests: a category spawns only when it has >= K grounding-quality profiles AND adequate range coverage, and the emission runs the full forge+gate+specialist-gate pipeline to EXIT=0
revisit_triggers: K or the coverage criteria are tuned
a category crosses the threshold or a spawned specialist underperforms

nodes.definition: Run the maintenance loop that keeps profiles from going stale: re-profiling triggers include new information (a claimed Google profile, a new license), business closure or relocation, ownership change (a new FBN filing), a service-line pivot, and simple data age (a profile past a staleness horizon re-verifies its load-bearing fields). Each trigger routes the affected profile back through the relevant capture nodes and the QA gate, and a closure or major change can ripple into the category aggregation and a spawned specialist's grounding.

included: re-profiling triggers (new info, closure, ownership change, staleness)
routing back through capture and the gate

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a re-profiling trigger fires or the staleness horizon is tuned

pros.claim: A staleness horizon plus event triggers keeps the catalog and its benchmarks current without re-doing everything
pros.example: a new FBN filing flagging an ownership change that re-opens just the ownership and economics fields

cons.claim: Over-frequent re-profiling burns research effort on businesses that have not actually changed
cons.example: re-verifying a stable 40-year shop every quarter for no new information

failure_modes: letting closed businesses linger as active in the catalog
a change rippling into a specialist's grounding without re-gating
acceptance_tests: each re-profiling trigger (new info, closure, ownership change, pivot, staleness) routes the profile back through the right capture nodes and the QA gate, and closures propagate to aggregation
revisit_triggers: the staleness horizon is tuned
a closure or ownership change is detected

nodes.definition: Enforce the hard guardrail under all economic modeling: per-business revenue and profit for private shops are NOT public, so the methodology never states a dollar figure for a named business as fact, only as a labeled benchmark estimate with confidence and a confirmation path. Only public business data is used — FBN filings, license registries, Google/social profiles, assessor parcels — and no private or personal data on owners beyond public records. This node is a constraint that dominates the revenue and cost nodes; any unlabeled figure or private-data use is a defect they must not commit.

included: no personal owner data beyond public records

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the financial-honesty or public-data policy changes

pros.claim: A single explicit guardrail prevents the most damaging failure mode — fabricated financials presented as fact
pros.example: blocking 'Shop X earns $1.2M' and forcing 'estimated $0.9-1.4M band, low confidence, would be confirmed by sales-tax data'

cons.claim: The guardrail makes every economic statement hedged, which can frustrate a reader wanting a single number
cons.example: a stakeholder who wants a point revenue figure the protocol will never provide

failure_modes: a revenue or cost figure slipping through unlabeled
scraping private or personal owner data to sharpen an estimate
acceptance_tests: no named-business dollar figure appears as fact anywhere; all are labeled estimates with confidence and a confirmation path, and only public data sources are used
revisit_triggers: a new public financial data source becomes available
the labeling or data-source policy changes

edges.why_related: the schema is the concrete instrument that realizes the profiling goal
service lines fill the schema's offerings section
ownership and longevity fill their schema section
size signals fill the schema's size section
the online block is a schema section the channel-mix capture fills
the guardrail is declared as a schema-level constraint before any economics field is filled
the input pattern is derived from what the business sells
which licenses apply follows from the service lines/trade
the customer base is read partly from the product/service mix
supplier identification localizes the abstract input pattern
size scales which supplier tier (cash-and-carry vs full distributor) is plausible
review volume and hours inform the demand read
the demand cycle refines the customer-demand picture over the year
positioning depends on which customers the business draws
size signals are the multiplicand against the revenue benchmark
seasonality adjusts a snapshot into an annualized revenue band
demand draw adjusts the volume side of the revenue band
the revenue band must obey the no-stated-fact guardrail
the margin benchmark is applied against the revenue band
provenance of the ownership/longevity fields feeds the confidence block
each size signal's source sets its field confidence
named-vs-typed supplier inference strength sets that field's confidence
the revenue band's confidence is part of the profile confidence block
public-license corroboration raises identity/category field confidence
low-confidence and missing fields are recorded as explicit unknowns
the profile confidence rollup is a gate input
the size and content of the unknowns register affect the publish/grounding verdict
a labeled cost/margin block is part of an economically complete profile
a sourced positioning field is part of profile completeness
only profiles passing the gate enter category aggregation
aggregation quality and count drive the spawn decision
closures and changes ripple from maintenance into the aggregation
refined local benchmarks feed back to tighten individual revenue bands
a re-profiling trigger re-runs service-line capture
an ownership-change trigger re-runs the ownership capture
the drive to produce a usable revenue band competes with the honesty of marking it largely unknown when size signals are thin
edges.resolution_rule: emit the band only at the confidence the size signals support; when signals are too thin for a useful band, record revenue as an unknown with the band tagged very-low confidence rather than implying false precision

edges.why_related: a strict publish gate that demands fresh sourcing competes with maintenance throughput across a large catalog
edges.resolution_rule: let the staleness horizon and event triggers, not a blanket re-gate, decide which fields re-verify; only load-bearing fields past the horizon force a full re-pass

edges.why_related: pressure to spawn a specialist quickly competes with the gate's insistence on grounding-quality coverage
edges.resolution_rule: spawn only on grounding-quality count AND range coverage; never lower the per-profile gate to reach the spawn threshold faster

edges.why_related: naming a specific supplier is more useful but riskier than a safe typed candidate
edges.resolution_rule: name a specific supplier only at a confidence its evidence supports; otherwise record a typed candidate at medium-low confidence and add it to the unknowns register

edges.why_related: aggregating real local profiles causally refines the trade cost/margin benchmark used per profile

conflict_axes.name: usefulness_vs_honest_uncertainty
conflict_axes.description: Producing a confident, usable profile competes with honestly recording how much could not be verified.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: state every field at the confidence its evidence supports and push the rest to the unknowns register rather than overclaiming

conflict_axes.name: benchmark_estimate_vs_stated_fact
conflict_axes.description: A reader wants a single revenue number, but private revenue is not public and may only be a labeled band.
poles: give only a labeled benchmark band
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: never state a named-business figure as fact; always emit a labeled band with confidence and a confirmation path

conflict_axes.name: named_supplier_vs_typed_candidate
conflict_axes.description: Naming a specific supplier is more useful but riskier than recording a safe typed candidate.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: name only at the confidence the evidence supports; otherwise a typed candidate at lower confidence plus an unknowns entry

conflict_axes.name: depth_per_profile_vs_coverage_throughput
conflict_axes.description: Deep grounding-quality profiles compete with covering more businesses faster.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold grounding-quality depth for profiles that will ground a specialist; allow lighter provisional profiles for breadth

conflict_axes.name: online_signal_vs_offline_reality
conflict_axes.description: Online footprint is easy to read but undercounts durable offline-only Valley businesses.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat digital absence as a channel fact, not a business-weakness fact; corroborate size and demand offline

conflict_axes.name: spawn_speed_vs_grounding_quality
conflict_axes.description: Spawning a category specialist sooner competes with waiting for representative, high-quality coverage.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: gate the spawn on quality count plus range coverage; never lower the per-profile gate to spawn faster

conflict_axes.name: public_data_only_vs_richer_private_data
conflict_axes.description: Private or personal owner data would sharpen a profile but is out of bounds.
poles: use any data that sharpens the profile
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use only public business-registration and observable data; never collect private or personal owner data

conflict_axes.name: snapshot_speed_vs_seasonal_accuracy
conflict_axes.description: A single-visit snapshot is fast but a seasonal trade needs an annualized view.
poles: adjust for the full seasonal cycle
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: adjust any size/demand snapshot by the trade's known seasonality before annualizing an estimate

conflict_axes.name: individual_profile_vs_category_aggregate
conflict_axes.description: Per-business benchmarks compete with aggregate benchmarks refined across the category.
poles: use the locally refined category benchmark
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: start from generic benchmarks, then let aggregation feed locally refined ones back into each profile

conflict_axes.name: profile_stability_vs_freshness
conflict_axes.description: Leaving a profile stable is cheap but data goes stale; re-profiling everything is wasteful.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: re-verify only load-bearing fields past the staleness horizon or on an event trigger, not the whole profile

edge_cases.description: A named business's exact revenue is requested and a single figure is expected
edge_cases.trigger: a stakeholder asks 'how much does Shop X make'
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse a stated figure; return a labeled benchmark band with confidence and the confirmation path (e.g. sales-tax permit, owner interview)

edge_cases.description: An FBN re-filing makes a long-running business look newly founded
edge_cases.trigger: the most recent FBN date is years after the true founding
edge_cases.mitigation: bracket age with the earliest corroborating signal (first review, 'since YYYY') and flag the FBN date as a re-filing

edge_cases.description: A delivery-truck photo names a one-off supplier mistaken for the standing one
edge_cases.trigger: a single review photo shows a distributor logo
edge_cases.mitigation: record it as a low-confidence candidate unless corroborated by repeated evidence; add to the unknowns register

edge_cases.description: A storefront's large footprint is mostly storage, inflating a revenue-per-sqft estimate
edge_cases.trigger: satellite footprint far exceeds visible selling area
edge_cases.mitigation: estimate productive/selling area separately or down-weight the sqft signal and lower the band confidence

edge_cases.description: A peak-season snapshot is annualized into an overstated revenue band
edge_cases.trigger: size or demand observed during the trade's seasonal peak
edge_cases.mitigation: apply the trade's seasonal adjustment before annualizing and note the observation month

edge_cases.description: A durable offline-only business looks weak from a thin digital footprint
edge_cases.trigger: unclaimed Google profile and no website for an established shop
edge_cases.mitigation: corroborate size and demand from offline signals and longevity; treat digital absence as a channel fact

edge_cases.description: Review-author geography biases the local-vs-regional demand read
edge_cases.trigger: demand draw inferred mainly from who posts reviews
edge_cases.mitigation: treat reviewer geography as one weak signal; corroborate with product mix, hours, and wholesale/catering cues

edge_cases.description: A profile passes on count but a category's sample is skewed to easy-to-profile businesses
edge_cases.trigger: the K easiest profiles are all one price tier or sub-type
edge_cases.mitigation: require range coverage (price tier and sub-type spread), not just count, before spawning

edge_cases.description: A business has closed but still appears active in the catalog
edge_cases.trigger: reviews stop and the profile shows 'permanently closed'
edge_cases.mitigation: mark closed, exclude from active benchmarks, and propagate the change to aggregation and any spawned specialist

edge_cases.description: A cottage-food or home-based operator has almost no public footprint and fails the gate despite being real
edge_cases.trigger: no FBN, no license, sparse profile for a real micro-business
edge_cases.mitigation: publish as provisional with a populated unknowns register; exclude from specialist-grounding until corroborated

edge_cases.description: A margin benchmark implies an impossible profit for the estimated revenue
edge_cases.trigger: the cost/margin band cannot reconcile with the revenue band
edge_cases.mitigation: treat the mismatch as a flag that a size signal is overstated; re-check the size vector and lower confidence

edge_cases.description: A business straddles two categories and the single service-line section fits poorly
edge_cases.mitigation: record both line sets with core/peripheral tags and note multi-category for the taxonomy and aggregation

workflow.action: State the profiling goal and research-artifact stance
workflow.description: Fix the dual purpose and the per-claim source-and-confidence rule before capture
workflow.gate: the dual purpose and the source-and-confidence rule are stated

workflow.description: Lay out every required section with empty fields marked unknown
workflow.gate: all required sections are present and the empty-becomes-unknown rule is set

workflow.action: Declare the financial-honesty and public-data guardrail
workflow.description: Bind all economics to labeled estimates and public-data-only sourcing
workflow.gate: the no-stated-private-financials and public-data-only rules are recorded

workflow.action: Capture service lines, ownership/longevity, size, online, and regulatory fields
workflow.description: Source the observable capture fields with provenance
workflow.gate: service lines are sourced and tagged and at least three size signals are recorded with sources

workflow.action: Model the supply chain by trade and localize suppliers
workflow.description: Derive the input pattern then identify named or typed-candidate suppliers
workflow.gate: each major input has a named or typed-candidate supplier with a confidence

workflow.action: Characterize demand, seasonality, and competitive position
workflow.description: Read the customer base, demand cycle, and differentiation
workflow.gate: B2C/B2B mix, draw, seasonality, and a provisional positioning are recorded with evidence

workflow.action: Estimate revenue as a labeled band and a cost/margin benchmark
workflow.description: Multiply benchmarks by size signals, adjust for season and demand, emit labeled bands
workflow.gate: a low-mid-high revenue band tagged 'estimate, not actual' with confidence and a confirmation note exists, sanity-checked against a labeled margin band

workflow.action: Score per-field and per-profile confidence with provenance
workflow.description: Tag each field's confidence and source and roll up weakest-link
workflow.gate: every field has a confidence tier and source tag and the profile confidence is the weakest load-bearing field

workflow.description: Record each unverified field with what was tried and what would close it
workflow.gate: every material unverified field is listed with its closing evidence

workflow.action: Run the profile QA acceptance gate
workflow.description: Issue pass/provisional/fail and decide grounding eligibility
workflow.gate: a verdict against the explicit criteria is recorded and grounding-eligibility is set

workflow.action: Aggregate passing profiles into category insight
workflow.description: Roll up distributions, supplier hubs, and refined benchmarks
workflow.gate: distributions, supplier hubs, and a refined benchmark with sample size are reported

workflow.action: Spawn a category specialist when thresholds are met, else maintain
workflow.description: On >= K grounding-quality profiles plus coverage, emit the specialist via the FACTORY pipeline; otherwise run the maintenance loop
workflow.gate: either the spawn runs the full forge+gate+specialist-gate to EXIT=0, or a maintenance pass with re-profiling triggers is recorded

priority_rationale: The goal, schema, and financial-honesty guardrail come first because they constrain every field that follows; observable capture (service lines, ownership, size, online, regulatory) precedes modeling (supply chain, demand, seasonality, position) which precedes the labeled economics; confidence scoring, the unknowns register, and the QA gate close each profile; and aggregation, spawn, and maintenance compose passing profiles into category knowledge and self-correcting upkeep, so the irreversible spawn step stands solely behind the quality gate and aggregation.

dominance_rules.rule: The financial-honesty guardrail dominates every economic field
dominance_rules.rationale: a single fabricated financial fact is more damaging than any missing estimate
dominance_rules.trigger: any revenue, profit, or cost figure for a named business is about to be recorded
dominance_rules.action: force a labeled estimate band with confidence and confirmation path, or mark it unknown; never state it as fact

dominance_rules.rationale: sharper estimates never justify collecting private or personal owner data
dominance_rules.trigger: a private or personal data source would improve a field
dominance_rules.action: reject the private source and rely on public business data and labeled inference

dominance_rules.rationale: an unsourced claim cannot be audited or weighted in aggregation
dominance_rules.trigger: a field is about to be recorded without a source tag
dominance_rules.action: attach a source and confidence or move the field to the unknowns register

dominance_rules.rationale: averaging hides a single load-bearing guess behind several solid fields
dominance_rules.trigger: a profile confidence is being rolled up
dominance_rules.action: set it to the weakest load-bearing field's confidence, not the mean

dominance_rules.rule: Grounding-quality coverage dominates raw spawn count
dominance_rules.rationale: a specialist on a skewed sample is worse than no specialist
dominance_rules.trigger: a category reaches K profiles but coverage is skewed
dominance_rules.action: withhold the spawn until price-tier and sub-type range coverage is met

dominance_rules.rule: The QA gate dominates publication and the spawn count
dominance_rules.rationale: thin profiles must not corrupt benchmarks or ground a specialist
dominance_rules.trigger: a profile is about to publish or be counted toward a spawn
dominance_rules.action: only gate-passing profiles publish as grounding-quality; weaker ones are provisional only

dominance_rules.rule: Seasonality adjustment dominates a raw snapshot in annualizing
dominance_rules.rationale: a peak or trough snapshot annualizes to a badly wrong figure
dominance_rules.trigger: a size or demand snapshot is being annualized for a seasonal trade
dominance_rules.action: apply the trade's seasonal adjustment and note the observation month before annualizing

dominance_rules.rule: Observable size signals dominate the trade name in scaling
dominance_rules.rationale: the name often misstates a diversified or atypical operation
dominance_rules.trigger: an estimate is being scaled from the assumed trade alone
dominance_rules.action: scale from sourced size signals and actual service lines, not the name

anti_rework_rules.rule: Declare the financial-honesty guardrail before filling any economics field
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a stated dollar figure slipping in and having to be retracted and re-labeled later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Source service lines from menus/profiles/photos before modeling supply chain or revenue
anti_rework_rules.prevents: building a supply-chain and revenue model on a miscategorized trade

anti_rework_rules.rule: Record at least three size signals with sources before estimating revenue
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an unscalable revenue band that has to be rebuilt once size is finally captured

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tag every field's source and confidence at capture time, not retroactively
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an unauditable profile that must be re-sourced field by field before it can pass the gate

anti_rework_rules.rule: Populate the unknowns register as gaps are found, not at the end
anti_rework_rules.prevents: silently guessed fields that later fail the QA gate and force a redo

anti_rework_rules.rule: Apply seasonality before annualizing any snapshot
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an annualized band that must be recomputed once the seasonal shape is known

anti_rework_rules.rule: Check range coverage, not just count, before declaring a category spawn-ready
anti_rework_rules.prevents: spawning a specialist on a skewed sample and having to re-ground it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Mark closures and ownership changes immediately in maintenance
anti_rework_rules.prevents: benchmarks and a spawned specialist drifting on stale or defunct profiles

iteration_protocol.trigger: a category reaches K grounding-quality profiles with adequate range coverage
iteration_protocol.action: run the spawn protocol: forge and gate the three category KBs and the specialist via the FACTORY pipeline

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new passing profile is added to a category
iteration_protocol.action: re-aggregate distributions and benchmarks and feed refinements back to individual profiles

iteration_protocol.trigger: a confirming public data point (sales-tax permit, franchise disclosure) surfaces for a business
iteration_protocol.action: upgrade the revenue/economics field confidence and resolve the related unknown

iteration_protocol.trigger: an ownership change (new FBN) or service-line pivot is detected
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the affected capture fields and re-gate the profile
mark it, exclude from active benchmarks, and propagate to aggregation and any spawned specialist

iteration_protocol.trigger: a profile passes its staleness horizon
iteration_protocol.action: re-verify its load-bearing fields and re-gate

iteration_protocol.trigger: a supplier hub is identified across the category's profiles
iteration_protocol.action: localize the supplier inference in affected profiles and raise their supply-chain confidence
